title: Overland conveyor, belt rip at transfer chute
tests: Obvious physical cause (tramp steel) with system causes missing; no evidence linked on verified nodes.
summary: Belt on stockyard feed conveyor CV-210 was ripped about 6 m at the head chute transfer. A broken bucket tooth from the primary loader was found jammed in the chute. The tree says 'tramp steel' and stops. Nodes are marked verified with no evidence linked.

problem.title: Belt rip at head chute on stockyard feed conveyor CV-210
problem.whatHappened: On 2 Jul 2026 the belt on CV-210 was ripped by about 6 m longitudinally at the head chute. A steel bucket tooth about 300 mm long was found jammed across the chute skirts. The conveyor was stopped by the rip detection loop. Belt was spliced and the conveyor restarted after 22 hours.
problem.where: Head end transfer chute, impact zone, carry side of the belt.
problem.when: Night shift, ore from stockpile 3, loader operating on the feed hopper before the crusher.
problem.impact: Stockyard feed stopped for 22 hours; port ship loading drew down stockpile. Belt repair contractors called out.
problem.makeModel: 1,200 mm wide steel cord belt, 450 m centres
problem.duty: Ore from crusher to stockyard, 2,000 t/h, no standby

evidence.title: Ripped belt and the tooth in the chute
evidence.note: Tooth about 300 mm long, hardened steel, jammed across the skirts. Rip about 6 m long.

evidence.title: Overbelt magnet check
evidence.note: Magnet is a permanent type; surface had a layer of fines. Not tested after the event.

evidence.title: Belt rip detection log
evidence.note: Loop operated and tripped the belt within seconds of the rip starting.

evidence.title: Loader operator
evidence.note: Said the loader bucket had been 'working hard' that week on a hard face. No tooth inspection recorded.

Loader teeth are not inspected on a set routine, so wear and missing teeth go unseen
No bucket tooth wear check or replacement standard in the loader PM plan
No tramp metal protection test routine or ownership

capa.deteriorationReasoning: A tooth breaking off a bucket is damage we can prevent by inspecting and replacing teeth before they fail, and by catching tramp steel before the belt. It is not clear yet whether wear or impact caused it: check the broken tooth.

preventive.what: Inspect loader bucket teeth and adaptors for wear and missing teeth to a set wear limit
preventive.interval: each shift pre-start check, full measure every 250 hours run

preventive.what: Test overbelt magnet or metal detector with a test piece, and clean the magnet face
Review magnet or detector position and size for the belt width and burden
Tooth replacement standard with wear limit and a record
Hold a set of teeth and adaptors for the loader

capa.spares: Teeth and adaptors for the loader; name the part type, no part numbers.
capa.rollout: All other loaders and excavators feeding conveyors, and all conveyors fed through the same crusher without tramp metal protection.
unacceptable: Retrain loader operators as the only action
